proposals: PPAC should publish in its Ready Reckoner each state's full petrol VAT schedule, including fixed cesses and “whichever is higher” floor clauses, not only the headline rate, so estimates of what states lose from blending are not understated in states with layered levies.

The commercial-tax departments of Maharashtra and Karnataka, the two largest modelled losers, should publish annual petrol VAT collections with litres sold and SGST collected on ethanol, so the modelled E20 net losses of about ₹2,126 crore and ₹1,798 crore can be checked against treasury data.

The GST Council should commission and publish a study of the IGST settlement on interstate ethanol supply, by state, before any blend above E20 is notified, so the fiscal effect of surplus states like Maharashtra supplying deficit states like Tamil Nadu is measured rather than described.

The Department of Food and Public Distribution should publish state-wise built and commissioned distillery capacity beside its sanction register, so the gap between about 4,530 crore litres sanctioned and roughly 2,000 crore litres installed is visible state by state from a government source.
